title: [Automated] Draft docs (kgateway): chore: enables ordered ADS by default
body:
# Documentation triage 1 candidates, 1 triaged, 0 skipped. | Product | new-feature | | --- | --- | | kgateway | 1 | ## New surface: no page documents this yet ### [kgateway-dev/kgateway#14644](https://github.com/kgateway-dev/kgateway/pull/14644) — chore: enables ordered ADS by default - **Product:** kgateway (upstream) → `kgateway-dev/kgateway.dev` - **Docs version:** envoy/main - **Release note:** Changes default to ordered ADS delivery (the old behavior is achievable with KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS=false), preserving CDS, EDS, LDS, and RDS response order for same-snapshot busy-stream additions. - **Not tested:** no cluster was available, so every command in this diff is unrun — cluster probing disabled for this run
How this page was chosen - **Disposition:** `pr` - **Why:** - code-path rules name an editable target but no page mentions any identifier, so this is new surface rather than a change to something already documented - 3 of 3 candidate page(s) are named by a code-path rule, so a person already recorded that this code affects them and only the choice among them is open; the draft picks one and states which it rejected - **Candidate pages:** - `assets/kgw-docs/pages/install/advanced.md` (editable here) - `assets/kgw-docs/pages/setup/customize/options.md` (editable here) - `content/docs/envoy/main/install/advanced.md` (editable here)
### kgateway-dev/kgateway#14644 — chore: enables ordered ADS by default - **Product:** kgateway (upstream) → kgateway-dev/kgateway.dev - **Docs version:** envoy/main kgateway-dev/kgateway#14644 changes the controller's default Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS) delivery behavior. Ordered ADS delivery is now enabled by default, so Cluster Discovery Service (CDS), Endpoint Discovery Service (EDS), Listener Discovery Service (LDS), and Route Discovery Service (RDS) responses keep their order when one xDS snapshot adds resources to busy proxy streams. The controlling setting is `controller.extraEnv.KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS`, which can be set to `"false"` to restore the previous unordered behavior. Before this change, unordered ADS delivery was the default unless `KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS` was set to `"true"`.
How kgateway-14644 was drafted, and what was not verified ## kgateway-dev/kgateway#14644 — chore: enables ordered ADS by default - **Code PR:** https://github.com/kgateway-dev/kgateway/pull/14644 - **Code issue:** none linked - **Product:** kgateway (upstream) → kgateway-dev/kgateway.dev - **Docs version:** envoy/main - **Category:** new-feature / pr ### Plan, and what changed it - **Planned:** Document the new default for ordered ADS delivery and the `KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS=false` escape hatch on the advanced install settings page. - **Learned:** `assets/kgw-docs/pages/install/advanced.md` renders into older version trees, but `content/docs/envoy/main/install/advanced.md` is an editable authorized target scoped to the affected development tree. - **Did:** Added a main-only Ordered ADS delivery section to `content/docs/envoy/main/install/advanced.md` and wrote a proposed release note because the default behavior changed. ### Why a documentation change is necessary The release note and diff change `EnableOrderedAds` from default `false` to default `true`. The existing advanced settings page documents controller environment variables such as `KGW_XDS_FIRST_CONNECT_DELAY`, but it did not mention `KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS`. A reader who needs the previous ADS behavior would not know which Helm value to set. For candidate pages, `content/docs/envoy/main/install/advanced.md` fit because it is the main-tree advanced install settings page and already documents controller environment variables. I rejected `assets/kgw-docs/pages/install/advanced.md` because the item resolved only to `envoy/main`, while that shared asset renders into `2.2.x`, `2.3.x`, `latest`, and `main`. I rejected `assets/kgw-docs/pages/setup/customize/options.md` because it is about gateway proxy customization with GatewayParameters, not controller installation settings. ### What changed on disk `content/docs/envoy/main/install/advanced.md`: Added a section that explains the ordered ADS default, names `KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS`, and shows the Helm `controller.extraEnv` escape hatch. `.pr-triage/kgateway-14644/proposed-release-note.md`: Added a release-note entry because the change alters default runtime behavior. ### How to verify this change 1. Install or upgrade kgateway with default Helm values. ```sh helm upgrade -i kgateway oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway \ -n kgateway-system --create-namespace ``` 2. Confirm that the controller deployment does not need an explicit `KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS=true` value for ordered ADS delivery to be active. ```sh kubectl -n kgateway-system get deployment kgateway \ -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].env[?(@.name=="KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS")].value}' ``` With default values, the command returns no value because the controller setting defaults to `true`. 3. Apply the documented escape hatch and confirm that the controller deployment carries the value. ```sh helm upgrade -i kgateway oci://cr.kgateway.dev/kgateway-dev/charts/kgateway \ -n kgateway-system \ --set controller.extraEnv.KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS=false kubectl -n kgateway-system get deployment kgateway \ -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].env[?(@.name=="KGW_ENABLE_ORDERED_ADS")].value}' ``` The command shows `false`. ### Proposed release note Wrote `.pr-triage/kgateway-14644/proposed-release-note.md` because the change alters default runtime behavior even though the upstream label is `kind/cleanup`. ### Style review Ran the structure, STE, shortcode, and product-specific passes plus grep checks for `this`, `may`, documentation test markup, and rebase edits. No Vale pass: the target repository has no Vale configuration, and this repository's house style linter does not apply to it. One finding applied: kept the new section in the main wrapper instead of the shared asset so no version gate is needed. ### What was not verified The configuration was not applied to a cluster, so every command in this diff is unrun. Cluster access is deliberately disabled for this CI run, and the work-list records `test_env.state: unconfigured`.
